title: Logging & Monitoring
description: Add logging to your application for better observability.

slides.title: Why Log? 📝
slides.content:
# Logging Helps You

- Debug issues in production
- Track user activity
- Monitor performance
- Auditing

Python's built-in `logging` module is sufficient for most apps.

slides.title: Configuring Logging
slides.content:
```python
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

@app.get("/")
async def root():
    logger.info("Root endpoint called")
    return {"message": "Hello"}
```

You can also use middleware to log every request.

slides.title: Request Logging Middleware
slides.content:
```python
from fastapi import Request
import time

@app.middleware("http")
async def log_requests(request: Request, call_next):
    start = time.time()
    response = await call_next(request)
    process_time = time.time() - start
    logger.info(f"{request.method} {request.url.path} - {response.status_code} - {process_time:.3f}s")
    return response
```
slides.codeSnippet:
import logging
import time
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request

app = FastAPI()
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger("api")

@app.middleware("http")
async def log_requests(request: Request, call_next):
    start = time.time()
    response = await call_next(request)
    process_time = time.time() - start
    logger.info(f"{request.method} {request.url.path} -> {response.status_code} ({process_time:.2f}s)")
    return response
